evals.prompt: Analyze this framework execution module. Go beyond listing classes and functions: readers should understand what it does, how it works, why it is designed this way, and how to continue reading the source.
evals.expected_output: Choose the explanatory focus from the actual module: algorithm, numerical transformation, interface rules or stateful collaboration. Explain the problem, decisive operations, design rationale, result and limits around one central thesis. Follow the smallest real execution path using qualified symbols and a deduplicated path::qualified.symbol source route, without per-claim or per-hop line quotas. Explain state ownership and non-responsibilities when they are relevant.

evals.prompt: Trace this asynchronous distributed path. Explain when an RPC returns, when a Future or background job completes, when weights are published, and when the next request sees the result.
evals.expected_output: Record caller/callee, crossing objects, pre/post state and local/remote, sync/async, blocking/non-blocking semantics for relevant hops. Distinguish submission, execution completion and downstream visibility; identify the first real wait, business completion signal, partial side effects, cleanup and rollback capability.

evals.prompt: Analyze a training batch from dataset through controller and worker partitioning to result writeback, focusing on container and field transformations.
evals.expected_output: Track object identity, container type, tensor shape or schema, padding/chunk/concat/reorder, in-place mutation versus copying/sharing, owner changes, storage location and delayed writeback alongside control flow. Expand only transformations that actually exist.

evals.prompt: Write a concrete feature analysis of cache invalidation in an ordinary software framework. Explain why it exists, how its implementation works, and how to continue into source; avoid a function catalog.
evals.expected_output: Use feature-analysis: a compact problem paragraph, solution shape, benefits/costs/constraints, then the smallest example expanded to actual system placement. Explain each load-bearing component, design reason, relevant state/data/control change, result and boundary. Account for applicable latency, memory, I/O, compatibility or operational costs, without importing parallel training. Close a real multi-hop path with an ASCII caller tree and stable-symbol route.

evals.prompt: Analyze tensor parallelism in a training framework: explain one partitioned matrix multiplication, model-wide integration, required companion mechanisms, the complete training path and aggregate costs.
evals.expected_output: Replay a smallest matrix example showing partition axes, local computation, aggregation, choice and cost. Include at least one principle figure covering input layout, rank-local GEMM, communication/reconstruction and differing forward/backward transformations. Expand to load-bearing model components with explanation, rationale, result, cost and constraints. Follow forward, objective/loss, backward and gradient handoff. Give companions equal depth only where correctness, capacity or performance depends on them; reconcile compute, communication, memory and synchronization costs.

evals.prompt: Must a software-feature source analysis include a separate section for every possible companion capability and fixed CPU, network and accelerator-memory metrics?
evals.expected_output: Choose depth from actual operations rather than a fixed domain template. Explain existing cooperating mechanisms, why they combine, relevant boundaries and data/state handoff, and incremental cost. Select measured or source-supported dimensions from latency, throughput, CPU/accelerator work, memory, storage, network/I/O, synchronization, compatibility, implementation and operations. Do not create empty conditional sections.

evals.prompt: Review an EP feature page with a token-to-expert table, prose on AllGather/AllToAll/Flex, a caller tree, qualitative cost table and forward/backward prose, but no principle figure and no shared token example replayed per variant. Can it pass? Does the rule also cover PP, TP, CP and packed datasets?
evals.expected_output: Reject the algorithmic visual gate. Require at least one principle figure replaying concrete input through decisive transformation or timing, ownership/layout changes, local compute, actual communication/synchronization and reconstructed output. Distinct live data planes reuse the same input and separately explain work, communication, forward/backward differences and incremental costs; a clearly separated multi-lane figure can combine them. Caller trees, class diagrams, prose and tables are not substitutes. Ordinary CRUD, parameter validation and one-to-one forwarding without an algorithmic transform do not trigger this gate.

evals.prompt: Analyze a single-process packed-dataset algorithm that places variable-length logical samples into a fixed-capacity physical token buffer while maintaining boundaries, offsets and padding. There are no ranks or collectives. Is a principle figure required?
evals.expected_output: Require a principle figure because packing, boundary mapping and padding are non-identity transformations; distributed execution is not a prerequisite. Use named samples and lengths to replay placement, physical offsets, boundary metadata and padding through the packed buffer. Mark capacity invariants and waste costs. Do not invent ranks, collectives or parallel-distributed sections.

evals.prompt: Analyze a standalone lower_bound implementation as a concrete software feature. It is one pure function over a sorted array with duplicate values, a comparator, local interval variables and a returned insertion index. Explain the complete implementation and its limits.
evals.expected_output: Use the algorithm lens: explain the input contract, half-open or inclusive interval actually implemented, decisive branch/update rules, duplicate handling, shrinking interval, correctness and termination, edge cases and time/space costs. Replay one smallest example in a principle figure and follow exact source operations to the returned index. The public function is the complete integration boundary; do not invent persistent ownership, RPCs, a publication stage or a multi-hop caller tree. A design comparison must explain a real choice, not replace the update-rule proof.

evals.prompt: Explain a pure row-wise affine quantization function with scalar and SIMD paths: scale calculation, integer mapping and reconstruction error. It has no persistent state, worker processes, network or training backward pass.
evals.expected_output: Use the numerical lens: derive scale, zero point if present, clipping/rounding and reconstruction from the actual arithmetic; replay the same input row in a principle figure for scalar/SIMD paths. Trace reductions, conversion, layout/stores and tail handling; explain precision, constant/nonfinite-input handling and compute/memory cost from source or measurements. Discuss why the numerical rules are valid, not a fictitious rejected service design. No ownership/publication/communication/backward stages are required when absent.
